title: E2H sanitized public failure patterns v0.1

patterns.title: Valid workspace becomes unreachable after path-domain translation
patterns.scenario: An agent session is bound to a workspace in one filesystem namespace, but a later runtime maps that location into a different host-path namespace. The project still exists in its original environment, while command execution fails before launch because the translated working directory is invalid.
observable_signals: The workspace exists when inspected from its original execution environment.
The agent reports that the current working directory is missing before a command starts.
The path shown by the failing runtime belongs to a different filesystem namespace than the project.
patterns.expected_behavior: Classify the failure as an environment working-directory error and require an explicit workspace rebind or path correction before replaying commands.

patterns.title: Background agent loses executables available in an interactive shell
patterns.scenario: A long-running agent service starts with a narrower PATH than an interactive user shell. Commands that are installed and usable manually are therefore unavailable when the agent launches tools from the service environment.
observable_signals: A command resolves successfully in the user's interactive shell.
The same executable cannot be found when launched by the background agent service.
The failing process environment has a different executable search path than the interactive environment.
patterns.expected_behavior: Classify the launch as command-not-found, preserve the observed environment distinction, and repair dependency discovery or service PATH configuration instead of retrying the same command blindly.

patterns.title: Fixed wall-clock limit terminates valid long-running agent work
patterns.scenario: An agent gateway applies a fixed execution timeout intended to stop stuck sessions. Legitimate multi-step work can exceed that wall-clock budget, causing an otherwise progressing task to be interrupted and its remaining work to be lost.
observable_signals: The task is still making observable progress when the configured wall-clock deadline is reached.
Execution is interrupted by the timeout mechanism rather than by a task-level assertion.
The same workload can complete when given a larger declared time budget.
patterns.expected_behavior: Classify the result as a timeout against the declared resource budget and preserve enough timing evidence to distinguish a budget failure from an unexpected process exit.

patterns.title: Setup step assumes write access that a self-hosted runner does not have
patterns.scenario: A setup action running on a self-hosted machine attempts to create or modify files in a location owned by another account. The workflow has enough access to start but cannot complete the setup operation under the runner identity.
observable_signals: The process reaches a filesystem mutation step and receives an operating-system permission denial.
The target location is outside the writable ownership boundary of the runner identity.
Changing ownership, target location, or runner permissions changes the outcome without changing the task logic.
patterns.expected_behavior: Classify the failure as environment permission-denied and require an ownership, path, or runner-identity fix rather than treating it as a task assertion failure.

metadata.publication_policy: public-source references only; no raw issue text or logs
